title: Sung Tieu
bio: Sung Tieu (b. 1987, Hai Duong, Vietnam) is a Berlin-based artist whose multidisciplinary practice spans installation, sculpture, drawing, text, sound, and video. Her work investigates the psychological dimensions of power, exploring how bureaucratic and institutional systems shape subjectivity. Her current solo exhibitions include Ruin, the German Pavilion at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia; Inserzionia at Castello di Rivoli, Turin; and How is your day? at Emalin, London. Current group exhibitions include the 82nd edition of the Whitney Biennial, New York; Boros Collection #5 at Boros, Berlin; A Thousand Times Berlin, The Collection Hamburger Bahnhof – Nationalgalerieder Gegenwart, Berlin; and Asad Raza: Electricity at E-WERK Luckenwalde. Tieu’s work has been exhibited internationally, with presentations at Kunsthalle Bern, KW Institute for Contemporary Art (Berlin), Harvard Art Museums, Amant (New York), Mudam Luxembourg, MIT List Visual Arts Center (Cambridge), Lafayette Anticipations (Paris), Kunst Museum Winterthur, Jameel Arts Centre (Dubai), Haus der Kulturen der Welt (Berlin), Nottingham Contemporary, and Haus der Kunst (Munich). She has also participated in major biennials, including the14th Taipei Biennial (2025),15th Gwangju Biennale (2024),14th Shanghai Biennale (2023),34th Bienal de São Paulo(2021), and the4th Kyiv Biennial (2021)
